title: Soil Science
description: Studies soil as a living, reactive, spatially variable natural body that supports ecosystems, agriculture, water quality, climate regulation, and infrastructure—integrating formation, morphology, physics, chemistry, biology, fertility, mapping, degradation, contamination, geotechnical behavior, conservation, restoration, and field/lab practice.

topics.title: Soil as an Earth System: Functions, Scales, and Human Dependence
topics.description: Students learn why soils are living, reactive, spatially variable systems central to food, water, climate, biodiversity, and infrastructure.

children.title: Soil functions
children.description: The point is to understand soil as infrastructure for ecosystems and society.

children.title: Soil system boundaries
children.description: Students learn to analyze soil across pedons, hillslopes, watersheds, farms, and cities.

children.title: Human dependence
children.description: Soils support food, climate regulation, biodiversity, and built environments.

topics.title: Soil Formation, Weathering, Parent Materials, and Landscape Position
topics.description: This module explains how climate, organisms, relief, parent material, and time create soil profiles and variability.

children.title: Soil-forming factors
children.description: Formation factors explain why soils vary across landscapes and climates.

children.title: Weathering processes
children.description: Minerals and rocks become soil through physical, chemical, and biological alteration.

children.title: Landscape controls
children.description: Position on the landscape shapes drainage, erosion, deposition, and horizon development.

topics.title: Soil Morphology, Horizons, Classification, and Field Description
topics.description: Students learn to describe soil profiles, classify soils, and connect morphology to process and land use.

children.title: Soil horizons
children.description: Horizons record soil-forming processes and guide interpretation.

children.title: O, A, E, B, C, and R horizons
Field description
children.description: Students learn to observe soil systematically in pits, cores, and auger samples.

children.title: Roots, pores, mottles, and redox features
Classification systems
children.description: Classification organizes soil knowledge for mapping and management.

topics.title: Soil Texture, Structure, Porosity, Density, and Physical Properties
topics.description: This topic develops the physical framework controlling water, air, roots, traffic, and engineering behavior.

children.title: Texture
children.description: Texture controls water retention, nutrient holding, workability, and habitat.

children.title: Structure and aggregation
children.description: Soil structure determines how pores connect and how roots and water move.

children.title: Granular, blocky, platy, and prismatic structure
Porosity and density
children.description: Bulk density and pore space reveal compaction and physical quality.

topics.title: Soil Water, Infiltration, Aeration, and Unsaturated Flow
topics.description: Students study how water and gases move through soils and control plant, microbial, and watershed function.

children.title: Soil water retention
children.description: Water availability depends on pore size and matric forces.

children.title: Infiltration and drainage
children.description: Students learn how rainfall enters, moves through, or runs off soils.

children.title: Aeration and gas exchange
children.description: Air-filled pores control root respiration and microbial metabolism.

topics.title: Soil Chemistry, pH, Cation Exchange, Salinity, and Redox
topics.description: This module explains the chemical reactions that control fertility, metal mobility, acidity, salinity, and contaminant behavior.

children.title: pH and acidity
children.description: Soil pH controls nutrient availability, metal solubility, and microbial activity.

children.title: Exchange and sorption
children.description: Charged surfaces hold nutrients and contaminants.

children.title: Salinity and redox
children.description: Salt and electron-transfer conditions strongly affect plant growth and chemical mobility.

topics.title: Soil Organic Matter, Carbon Cycling, and Climate Feedbacks
topics.description: Students learn how organic matter drives soil structure, fertility, water retention, biodiversity, and carbon storage.

children.title: Organic matter pools
children.description: Organic matter exists in forms with different turnover and function.

children.title: Carbon cycling
children.description: Students connect decomposition, stabilization, and emissions.

children.title: Soil health effects
children.description: Organic matter improves structure, water, nutrient supply, and resilience.

topics.title: Soil Biology, Microbiomes, Food Webs, and Ecosystem Function
topics.description: This topic covers soil organisms as engines of decomposition, aggregation, nutrient cycling, and resilience.

children.title: Soil organisms
children.description: Students learn the roles of microbes, fauna, and roots in soil function.

children.title: Microbial processes
children.description: Microbes drive decomposition and nutrient transformations.

children.title: Soil food webs
children.description: Food-web structure links biodiversity to function and resilience.

topics.title: Plant Nutrition, Soil Fertility, and Nutrient Cycling
topics.description: Students connect nutrient supply, uptake, amendments, and losses to crop, ecosystem, and water-quality outcomes.

children.title: Essential nutrients
children.description: Fertility starts with knowing what plants need and how they acquire it.

children.title: Nutrient cycling
children.description: Nutrients move through organic, mineral, plant, and loss pathways.

children.title: Fertility management
children.description: Students learn to interpret tests and choose amendments responsibly.

topics.title: Soil Survey, Digital Soil Mapping, GIS, and Remote Sensing
topics.description: This module teaches students to interpret soil maps, spatial data, and landscape patterns for field and planning decisions.

children.title: Soil survey interpretation
children.description: Soil maps convert field observations into usable land information.

children.title: Digital soil mapping
children.description: Modern mapping combines field data, terrain, imagery, and models.

children.title: Remote sensing and GIS
children.description: Spatial tools help assess soil moisture, erosion, salinity, and land degradation.

topics.title: Soil Degradation, Erosion, Compaction, Salinization, and Desertification
topics.description: Students learn the major pathways by which soil function is lost and how to diagnose risk.

children.title: Erosion
children.description: Soil erosion removes productive surface soil and delivers sediment downstream.

children.title: Physical degradation
children.description: Compaction and structure loss reduce infiltration, rooting, and biological function.

children.title: Chemical and landscape degradation
children.description: Salinity, acidification, and desertification threaten long-term productivity.

topics.title: Contaminated Soils, Soil-Sediment Chemistry, and Remediation
topics.description: This topic integrates environmental chemistry with soil processes to evaluate pollutants, exposure, and cleanup strategies.

children.title: Contaminant behavior
children.description: Soil chemistry controls pollutant mobility, persistence, and exposure.

children.title: Risk and sampling
children.description: Students learn to connect concentration, exposure pathway, and uncertainty.

children.title: Remediation
children.description: Cleanup strategies depend on contaminant, soil, hydrology, and land use.

children.title: Excavation, capping, and monitored natural attenuation

topics.title: Soil Mechanics, Geotechnical Behavior, and Land-Use Constraints
topics.description: Students gain a practical bridge to soil strength, seepage, settlement, slopes, and site investigation.

children.title: Index and engineering properties
children.description: Civil and environmental decisions require soil behavior under load and water flow.

children.title: Stress, strength, and settlement
children.description: Students learn why soil can compress, fail, or stabilize structures.

children.title: Site investigation and hazards
children.description: Soil science supports safe siting and hazard reduction.

topics.title: Soil Management, Conservation, Restoration, and Regenerative Systems
topics.description: This module connects soil science to applied land stewardship, agriculture, restoration, and sustainability.

children.title: Conservation practices
children.description: Management can reduce erosion, improve water, and protect productivity.

children.title: Soil health systems
children.description: Regenerative practices aim to rebuild biological, physical, and chemical function.

children.title: Restoration and land rehabilitation
children.description: Damaged soils can be rebuilt, but recovery depends on constraints and goals.

topics.title: Soil Field, Lab, and Restoration Project
topics.description: The course culminates in a field-to-lab project that classifies, analyzes, maps, and recommends management for a real soil system.

children.title: Field investigation
children.description: Students practice professional field observation and sampling.

children.title: Laboratory and data analysis
children.description: The project connects measurements to interpretation.

children.title: Texture, pH, EC, organic matter, and nutrients
Management recommendation
children.description: The final deliverable turns soil evidence into a defensible action plan.
